mechanisms.name: Target scoring (no-target branch, main.go 7554-7624)
mechanisms.how: Score = -dist*4, +600 raiser, +150 elite; rabies-only terms (poison-state -300, +25 per uninfected neighbor within 10, poison-immune -500) gated on the *rabies FLAG being non-empty, not on the character actually knowing Rabies. Weaponless pile-shun (skip targets within 25 of corpseTargetPos unless already at arm's reach). 12s blacklist filter.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the shape, FIX the trigger. Score-over-nearest is correct and the raiser/elite/spread terms encode real tactical knowledge. But build-specific terms keyed to a launch-flag string (whose DEFAULT is 'f2' — every char gets rabies-shaped targeting unless the flag is explicitly blanked) is config leaking into tactics. Terms should attach to skill metadata resolved from the live capability model.

mechanisms.name: packAssess posture arithmetic (5380-5446)
mechanisms.how: Threat = count of enemies within 30, +2 elite, +2 raiser. Strength = pets*3 + 2 + level; bravery floor overrides to pets*3+14 if level<12 AND armed; weaponless collapses to pets*3+1; +2 if HP>60. Postures: threat>3x strength = regroup, threat>strength = kite, else engage. Shared by farm posture, travel opportunity gate, and corpse-approach don't-feed-the-camp check.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the single-authority pattern (one oracle, three consumers — that part is right). DISCARD the arithmetic: it is unitless folklore where every constant is a memorial to a specific death (the bravery floor to XP starvation, the weaponless collapse to five pile deaths). It cannot see monster DPS, damage type, ranged attackers, gear EHP, or the pack 35 tiles away that is about to matter. Each new death will demand another special-case constant forever.

mechanisms.name: Posture hysteresis (7514-7533)
mechanisms.how: A kite<->engage flip requires margin >= 4 or surviving a 1.2s dwell; regroup always applies immediately.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the concept (dwell + margin + fear-overrides-dwell is correct control theory) but recognize it as a low-pass filter over a NOISY SCALAR. With a calibrated threat model the noise shrinks and the filter can loosen.

mechanisms.name: Attack execution switch (7869-7966)
mechanisms.how: Four cases chosen by flag presence and a dead memory read: (1) spellCast = KeyBindings-derived bound spell, right-click at sx,sy; (2) useCast = *rabies flag, right-click at sx,sy; (3) *melee flag = press key, VERIFY RightSkill flipped to a hardcoded whitelist {Jab, PowerStrike, Throw}, then hover-confirmed right-click; (4) default = meleeSwing, hover-confirmed left interactClick. sx,sy are computed at line 7854 from the tick-start data snapshot (read at 5545) — potentially seconds stale after ~30 behavior blocks with embedded sleeps.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD as a structure. Cases 1-2 right-click STALE screen coordinates with zero hover confirmation — the air-punching lives here still; the 'hover-confirmed strikes' commit fixed only cases 3-4. Case 1 can never fire on 3.2 (KeyBindings reads dead) yet outranks case 2 in the switch. Each case independently reimplements a different subset of the correct pipeline.

mechanisms.name: hoverAim + meleeSwing (4700-4725)
mechanisms.how: moveStop, re-read LIVE position, sweep 25 hardcoded pixel offsets (dy {-12,0,-24,-36,8} x dx {0,±10,±20}) at 45ms each, return the point where HoverData.UnitID == target; meleeSwing clicks it via interactClick (VK_LBUTTON override), blind-clicks as last resort.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP — this is the one honest strike primitive (it obeys the measured hover law AND re-reads fresh data, the implicit admission that the tick snapshot is unfit for aiming). Flaws to fix in the redesign: up to 1.1s open-loop sweep during which combat stands frozen; pixel offsets assume one sprite size and ignore -dpiscale; the blind-click fallback silently converts a failed attack into a WALK order toward the pack.

mechanisms.name: fightThrough (4730-4755)
mechanisms.how: When nav is blocked and a hostile is within 8: press *rabies and right-click a computed screen point (no selection verify, no hover confirm), else meleeSwing.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the doctrine (monsters body-block but are absent from every collision source — violence IS the nav fallback; this obeys a measured law). DISCARD its private attack implementation — a fifth strike path with the weakest verification of all, which is exactly where a stale click matters most (you are wedged against the target).

mechanisms.name: Throw block (8023-8047)
mechanisms.how: Outside engage posture, dist<=22, 700ms cadence: verify a hand-slot stack holds >40 quantity, press *throwKey, VERIFY RightSkill==Throw, then right-click sx,sy.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the double closed loop (selection flip + quantity floor — both learned from real failure modes: weaponless leaves the skill red, quantity 0 vanishes the stack). But it clicks the same stale tick-start sx,sy unconfirmed, and it is a sixth hand-rolled strike path.

mechanisms.name: Curse pass (7884-7894)
mechanisms.how: Amp Damage via KeyBindings-derived curseKB on an 8s cooldown before attacking, right-click at stale sx,sy.
mechanisms.verdict: Conceptually sound (one curse multiplies the whole army), practically DEAD on 3.2 (KeyBindings) and unverified when alive (no selection readback, no hover). Fold into the unified layer as a skill-policy entry, not a bespoke block.

mechanisms.name: Damage watchdog (5366-5373, 7896-7917)
mechanisms.how: Track engaged target's Life; if it never drops for 8s, blacklist. On 3.2 Life reads FROZEN at 32768 (known law), so 'life < engagedLife' can never fire — the watchdog degenerates into a flat 8-second per-target timer, blacklisting any monster that legitimately takes >8s to kill (common for a low-level char in 12x density).
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the cause-agnostic give-up doctrine (catches immunities nobody predicted); DISCARD the sensor. Honest damage evidence on this build: target Mode transitions (GettingHit/death), poison state appearing, pet-swarm proximity, corpse appearing. A dead sensor wired to a live decision is worse than no watchdog — it manufactures false unkillables.

mechanisms.name: Blacklists (4442, 4494, 4502)
mechanisms.how: Three maps with two different value conventions: combat blacklist (value=set-time, 12s window), lootBlacklist (value=EXPIRY, 15/45/60s), objBlacklist (value=set-time, 60s). Written by five different code sites for three different reasons (unreachable, undamageable, click-failed) with the reason discarded.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD as separate ad-hoc maps; KEEP the memory. One outcome ledger keyed by UnitID with {reason, expiry}, written only by the strike/approach executors, read by all selectors. The reason matters: 'unreachable' should invalidate on MY position change; 'undamageable' should not.

mechanisms.name: deriveCombat per-tick capability read (534-590)
mechanisms.how: Re-derives ranged-ness (name-substring on ACTIVE hand slots — correct lesson from the swap-slot bug) and bound damage/curse skills (KeyBindings cross-checked against the known-Skills map) every tick. Class-keyed hardcoded candidate lists: necro {BoneSpear, Teeth}, amazon {Jab, PowerStrike}, nothing for the other five classes.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the philosophy — capabilities from live state, re-read every tick, binding trusted only if the skill is actually known (correct distrust of 3.2 memory). But it is a vestigial organ: its castKB output feeds only the never-firing spellCast case, while real combat runs on flags. The redesign should make this the ONLY authority and close its loop: learn key->skill mappings empirically (press, read RightSkill, record) instead of trusting either the dead KeyBindings block or launch flags.

mechanisms.name: Right-skill register discipline (summon 6250-6304, golem 6309-6319, throw, rabies, TP tome)
mechanisms.how: Every block that presses a skill hotkey mutates the shared right-skill slot and relies on the convention 'the next bite's -rabies press restores the attack skill'. Some paths verify the selection after pressing (melee, throw), most do not (rabies, summon, golem, curse, castSelf).
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD the convention. The right-skill slot is an unowned global register with implicit cross-block restore obligations; the near-miss where the leftover selection was the TP TOME (blind right-click would have cast a portal at a zombie) is the smoking gun. Every skill use must be select-verify-use-atomic inside one executor.

mechanisms.name: Summon/golem closed loops (6242-6319)
mechanisms.how: Summon: cast at nearest corpse, verify pet count rose, 5 fruitless casts disable 10min; army cap read LIVE from RaiseSkeleton level (+1 golem) with the flag demoted to floor-fallback. Golem: timer-based refresh at own feet.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP — this is the best-designed combat block in the file: closed-loop effect verification, live self-knowledge overriding config, failure hypothesis ('granting wand is on a corpse') encoded as a backoff. It is the template the strike layer should generalize.

mechanisms.name: Autoskill point spending (189, 6386-6456)
mechanisms.how: Build list 'tabX,tabY,skillX,skillY,skillID,max;...' in a flag string — hand-measured physical panel pixels from a live tree screenshot (skilldesc.txt consulted offline; nothing in code derives cells). Calm-gated, tab-then-icon uiClick, verified via SkillPoints readback, refused entries fall through within the same visit, tree closed by 't' toggle (esc = pause-menu trap, correctly avoided).
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the verification loop and the fall-through queue; DISCARD pixel coordinates as flag payload. Tree-cell positions are derivable data (class + tab + cell grid), and hand-measured pixels break on any resolution/DPI/UI-scale change. Same disease as -equipslots and -autostat: screen geometry as configuration.

mechanisms.name: Intent ledger vs combat (5337-5357, 7857-7864)
mechanisms.how: claim() grants the walk to one intent per hold window; combat claims at prio 50, 60 on contact; critloot 70 outranks a swing.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the arbitration idea — it is the embryo of the real fix for the 30-interleaved-blocks disease. In the redesign it should govern ALL effectors (walk, cursor, skill register), not just the walk, because the air-punching and the TP-tome near-miss are both cursor/register contention, which the ledger today does not arbitrate.

rootDefects.defect: Attack execution is six independent hand-rolled paths (spellCast, useCast/rabies, melee-hotkey, meleeSwing default, fightThrough, throw — plus curse), each implementing a different SUBSET of the verified strike pipeline. Which subset you get — and therefore whether the attack lands, walks, whiffs, or casts a town portal at a zombie — depends on which launch flags are non-empty and whether a dead memory block happens to parse.
rootDefects.evidence: main.go 7925-7966: spellCast and useCast right-click hid.Click(RightButton, sx, sy) with NO hover confirm and NO selection verify, while the melee case verifies RightSkill against a hardcoded whitelist AND hover-confirms, and the default meleeSwing hover-confirms. fightThrough (4745-4751) and the throw block (8038-8039) click the same unconfirmed coordinates. The 'Intelligence over orders: hover-confirmed strikes' commit fixed 2 of 6 paths — tonight's air-punching was the other 4.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: The pipeline steps that make a strike honest — moveStop, select-skill, VERIFY selection took, fresh-read aim, HoverData confirm, button-specific click mechanics, post-click outcome observation — were each discovered in a different path's incident and patched into that path only. There is no shared strike executor, so every lesson must be re-learned per path; correctness is a property of the code path, not of the system. The unified layer is one Strike(target, skillIntent) executor that always runs the full pipeline: resolve skill->key from a LEARNED mapping (press key, read back Left/RightSkill, record — self-calibrating around the dead KeyBindings block); select and verify or abort WITHOUT clicking; aim via hoverAim on fresh reads within a time budget; click with the mechanics that button needs (left = VK_LBUTTON override, right = message click — both measured laws); then observe outcome (Mode change, poison state, pet count, quantity decrement) and write one outcome ledger that feeds targeting, watchdogs, and blacklists.

rootDefects.defect: Build identity and combat semantics live in launch-flag strings with class-specific DEFAULTS (-rabies defaults to 'f2', -werewolf 'f1', -spirit 'f3'), while the live capability model (deriveCombat) exists but is subordinate — its output feeds only the branch that can never fire on 3.2.
rootDefects.evidence: Line 182: rabies flag default 'f2' on a supposedly generic bot; 7871: useCast = *rabies != '' (flag presence = attack doctrine); 7597: targeting's poison-spread scoring gated on the same flag; 574-577: dmgSkills hardcoded for exactly two classes; 572: comment admitting 'in practice the -melee/-rabies flag paths carry combat' because the binding block reads dead.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: There are two competing sources of truth for 'what can this character do' — frozen launch config and live memory — and the frozen one wins. That is the same disease as the bow that left with the user while -attackrange 25 kept sniping with a stick, which deriveCombat was BUILT to cure and then wasn't allowed to. Skill semantics (spreads-poison, needs-corpse, is-curse, ammo-consuming) belong to skill metadata resolved against the live Skills map; keys belong to an empirically learned key->skill table; flags should carry nothing but preferences.

rootDefects.defect: One perception snapshot per tick (d, me at 5545-5546) feeds decisions executed seconds later, after ~30 sequential behavior blocks with embedded sleeps. Every world-click coordinate computed from that snapshot (sx,sy at 7854 for rabies/spell/curse/throw) is a bet that nothing moved in a 12x-density brawl.
rootDefects.evidence: sx,sy computed at 7854 from tick-start data; the bite log (7922-7924) even labels tick-start HoverData the 'AIM ORACLE' — explicitly the verdict on the PREVIOUS tick's aim. hoverAim (4702) quietly re-reads gr.GetData() mid-sweep because its author knew the snapshot was stale — the exception that indicts the rule.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: A single-snapshot-then-act-blindly tick model is fine for slow intents (drink, panel) and fatal for aiming at moving units. The redesign needs two data tiers: a cheap fresh read at every aim/click point (the hover primitives already prove this works), and the tick snapshot reserved for planning. This falls out naturally once strikes go through one executor that owns its own reads.

rootDefects.defect: The right-skill slot is an unowned global register: seven blocks mutate it (rabies, melee, throw, summon, golem, curse, TP tome) and consistency depends on the documented convention that 'the next bite's -rabies press restores the attack skill'.
rootDefects.evidence: 6244 and 6308: the restore convention stated in comments; 7942-7946: the observed failure — with no javelin the F1 press fails SILENTLY, the register keeps its last value, and once that value was the TP TOME; a blind right-click would have cast a portal mid-fight. Verification of the register exists in exactly two of the seven writers.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Cross-block invariants held together by comments are how a 7000-line single loop fails. The register needs an owner: the strike executor selects, verifies, uses, and is the ONLY writer; anything needing a skill goes through it. This also makes 'selection failed' a first-class capability signal (no javelin, wand on a corpse) instead of a silent whiff.

rootDefects.defect: The posture model is unitless incident-driven arithmetic: threat and strength are magic-constant tallies (w=1/+2/+2 within radius 30; pets*3+2+level; floor 14 if young-and-armed; 1 if weaponless; +2 above 60% HP; regroup at 3x), each constant added after a specific death or starvation.
rootDefects.evidence: 5380-5446 with its own comments narrating the fossil record: the petless-melee misread (run 1), the bravery floor (330 xp in 5.5 min of flapping), the weaponless collapse (five deaths at the pile camp). The hysteresis block (7520-7528) exists solely because the scalar flips 12x/s at the boundary — a filter over noise the model itself generates.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: It is curve-fitting to yesterday's corpses, not a model. It has no damage dimension (a ranged pack and a melee pack of equal count read identically), no time dimension (threat 30 tiles away is invisible until it isn't), and no gear dimension beyond armed/not. Keep packAssess's single-authority position; replace its internals with quantities that have units — expected incoming DPS vs EHP+sustain, expected kill rate vs pack size — calibrated from the outcome ledger the strike executor writes, so the next death tunes a parameter instead of spawning a special case.

rootDefects.defect: Dead sensors remain wired to live decisions: the KeyBindings block (known dead on 3.2) still selects the top attack-switch branch, and the frozen Life stat still drives the damage watchdog, which therefore degenerated into a flat 8s timer that blacklists slow-but-winnable fights.
rootDefects.evidence: 7872/7926: spellCast branch fed by prof.hasCast from KeyBindings; 7904-7908: comment admitting Life is frozen at 32768 and that the watchdog's life-drop reset can never fire, patched by excusing it as 'only catches genuinely unkillable targets' — untrue for a level-4 char needing >8s per tough monster in 12x density.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: The codebase has a sensor-health doctrine (the frozen-Life lesson, the bindings distrust in deriveCombat) but no mechanism: nothing marks a data source untrusted and quarantines its consumers. A redesigned reader layer should carry per-field validity verdicts (probed at startup: does Life move? does KeyBindings parse against known skills?) so decision code branches on 'sensor honest?' explicitly instead of each block privately remembering which fields lie.

keep: hoverAim / HoverData.UnitID confirmation as the universal aim oracle — promoted from 'fix applied to two paths' to a mandatory stage of the single strike executor (it already embodies two measured laws: hover is the only honest will-this-click-hit, and aiming requires fresh reads)

Closed-loop selection verification (press key -> read RightSkill -> act only on match) from the melee and throw paths — generalized to every skill use, and inverted into a startup/runtime PROBE that LEARNS the key->skill map empirically, retiring the dead KeyBindings dependency entirely
The summon block's full closed loop (cast -> verify pet count -> hypothesis-tagged backoff) and live army cap from skill level — the template for effect-verified skill use

packAssess as a single shared authority consumed by posture, travel gate, and corpse approach — keep the topology, replace the arithmetic with unit-bearing quantities calibrated from recorded fight outcomes
Posture hysteresis (dwell + margin, fear overrides dwell) and the contact override/exemption doctrine (nothing at arm's reach is ever shunned or outwalked)
Score-based target selection over nearest-first, with raiser-first and spread-aware terms — re-homed onto skill metadata instead of flag presence
Cause-agnostic damage watchdog doctrine — rebuilt on honest sensors for this build (target Mode transitions, poison state application, corpse appearance) instead of the frozen Life stat
Weaponless cowardice and gear hunger as capability-derived behavior changes (the CONCEPT: posture follows what the character actually holds, re-read live)
Throw's double closed loop (selection flip + quantity floor) as skill metadata: ammo-consuming skills declare their resource and floor
moveStop-before-any-aim discipline (held force-move turns every cursor aim into a walk order — measured law, correctly threaded through every input wrapper)
Autoskill/autostat SkillPoints/StatPoints readback verification and the refused-entry fall-through queue

The intent ledger (claim) as the arbitration seed — extended to own ALL effectors (walk, cursor, skill register), which dissolves the interleaved-blocks contention that produced both the air-punching and the TP-tome near-miss
fightThrough's doctrine that violence is the nav fallback for body-blocking monsters absent from all collision data (measured law) — re-implemented as a normal strike-executor call
The calm gates (anyEnemyWithin) on panel-opening activities, and the 't'-toggle tree close (the esc pause-menu trap is real)
discard: The four-case attack switch and its satellite strike sites (fightThrough's private rabies click, the throw block's click, the curse pass) — all replaced by one Strike(target, skillIntent) executor running the full select/verify/aim/confirm/click/observe pipeline

Launch flags as build identity: class-specific hotkey defaults ('f2' rabies on every char), flag-presence-driven attack doctrine (useCast = flag != ''), and flag-gated targeting semantics — replaced by a live capability model + skill metadata + learned key map
All world-clicks at tick-start sx,sy coordinates — every aimed click must be computed from a fresh read inside the executor
The spellCast branch fed by the dead-on-3.2 KeyBindings block, and any decision consuming an unquarantined dead sensor without an explicit validity verdict
The Life-stat damage watchdog as implemented (frozen sensor + flat 8s timer masquerading as damage tracking)
The unowned right-skill register and the 'next bite restores the attack skill' cross-block convention
packAssess's magic-constant internals (pets*3+2+level, the 14 floor, the 3x regroup multiplier, +2 HP bonus) as unitless incident fossils
Three inconsistent blacklist maps with mixed value conventions — replaced by one reason-coded outcome ledger written solely by executors
Hand-measured physical-pixel panel coordinates as flag payload (autoskill tree cells, autostat buttons, equipslots) — derive from panel geometry + calibration probe, store per-resolution
hoverAim's fixed pixel sweep offsets (sprite-size and DPI assumptions) and its silent blind-click fallback that converts a failed attack into a walk toward the pack
The hardcoded acceptable-skill whitelist {Jab, PowerStrike, Throw} and the two-class dmgSkills lists — subsumed by skill metadata keyed off the live Skills map
Priority-by-source-order of the ~30 interleaved blocks as the de facto combat scheduler — the ledger, not file position, should decide who owns the character
